name: Whatnot turntable v2 - crown drive
goal: Slimmest practical 12 V card turntable: N20 gearmotor lying flat, spur pinion into a printed crown gear on a fixed axle, two 608s stacked inside the rotating parts.
requirements: Motor horizontal; right-angle stage = printed spur pinion + printed crown (face) gear on the vertical axis
Base height under 30 mm, overall under 40 mm with the plate
Plate 2–5 RPM adjustable from a panel knob; rocker switch spin / hold
Fixed axle: the plate and gear rotate on bearings, no printed face rubs under load
Every part prints flat without supports on the H2S (350 x 320 x 325 mm); plate in one piece
Assembly: no glue, no soldering except motor leads, one strap screw pair, six lid screws, three plate screws

hardware.part: GA12-N20 12 V gearmotor, 20 RPM (15 or 30 also work), 3 mm D-shaft
hardware.critical_dims: 12x10 body, gearbox 12 + can 15.5, shaft 3 D x 10

hardware.part: PWM DC speed controller 12 V >= 1 A with panel pot

mechanism.train: N20 (20 RPM) -> 12T pinion m1 -> 42T crown gear (3.5:1) -> hex coupling -> hub -> plate
mechanism.axle: fixed printed post d7.85 (or 8 mm steel rod); crown and hub each carry a 608 on it
mechanism.load_path: plate -> hub ledge -> hub 608 outer race -> inner race -> spacer tube -> crown 608 inner race -> floor ring -> base
mechanism.torque_path: crown hex boss -> hub hex socket -> 3 screws -> plate

parts.name: crown
parts.orientation: teeth up, bearing pocket at the bed

parts.name: hub
parts.orientation: flange down, pockets open up (selector flips)

steps.done_when: base height < 30 and total < 40 (CHECK base_height, total_height)
pinion axis at crown pitch plane + pinion pitch radius; crown/pinion interference empty
plate weight reaches the base through two 608 inner races and the spacer, never a printed face
motor, PCB, panel parts inside inner_r; lid lip notched at bosses

applied_lessons.lesson: Right-angle drives for FDM: use a crown (face) gear + spur pinion, not a bevel pair; it prints teeth-up with no overhang and tolerates +-0.5 mm axial pinion position.
Sink the lid bearing boss into a recess in the drive gear: it saves ~4 mm of base height versus stacking bearing above gear.
Orient a gearmotor tangentially (can along the base's circumference) so the base diameter is set by the plate gear, not by motor length.
Slimmest vertical-axis stack: fixed post, one bearing inside each rotating part, spacer tube between inner races; height is then set by the pinion OD, not by bearing stacking.
Build round plates and rims as one rotate_extrude() profile; a union of coincident cylinders leaves a 4-face seam edge and a non-watertight STL.
Pocket ceilings printed face-down are flat overhangs the area metric under-reports: give pockets 45 deg conical walls and keep any remaining bridge under ~30 mm.
Run an interference view (intersection() of every assembled pair, must be empty) before shipping: a lid locating lip crossing the screw bosses is invisible in renders but shows as ~120 mm3 overlap.
When a pinion meshes a crown/face gear on its centre line, phase the pinion by half a tooth pitch (180/N degrees) or tooth lands on tooth; the interference view catches it.
Keep >= 2 mm between a rotating disc rim and any static wall; a 0.5 mm graze shows up as <1 mm3 in the interference view but will click when printed.
A part with features on both faces (boss below, hub above) cannot print flat: split the smaller feature into its own part (e.g. a spacer ring) instead of adding supports.
Arched clamps/straps print on their side as a 2-D profile; standing them up makes the crown a 90 deg overhang.

open_questions: Measure the N20: gearbox length varies with ratio (9-12 mm); set n20_gb_len.
PWM board must be under 16 mm tall (2.4 floor + 1 tape + 1.6 PCB + 16 = 21 < lid 23).
